# Release Notes - awake 1.0.0

Release date: 2026-10-24 Package: `awake-daemon.win64.zip`

The first stable release of **awake**, a Windows command line tool that keeps
the system awake. It ships the complete feature set that was staged through
0.7.0-beta and 0.8.0-beta-pre1.0.0, now without the pre-release suffix and
covered by a compatibility promise.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This project is generated by AI and has not been extensively reviewed. Please scrutinize the code carefully before use. The author is not responsible or liable for any consequences arising from the use of this software.

## What 1.0 means

- **Stable command line and protocol.** Existing commands, aliases, options, status keys and wire verbs keep their meaning. Adding things is still possible in a minor release; removing or renaming them now requires a major version bump. The promise is spelled out in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- **Distribution stays .zip only.** Both executables are statically linked and self-contained; there is still no installer, no winget or Scoop manifest and no code signing certificate. Those are planned for a later release.
- **Fixes over features.** Bug fixes and hardening take priority over new functionality from here on.

## Highlights

- **Keep-awake and screen keep-awake** with optional time limits: `awake 1 for 30m`, `awake 1 until 18:00`, `awake screen on for 2h`. The daemon measures expiry on a monotonic clock, so changing the system time or crossing a daylight saving boundary cannot move the end point.
- **Power event awareness**: on resume from sleep or hibernation the daemon immediately re-applies the execution state, and `awake status` shows how long ago the last resume was handled.
- **Script-friendly output** (`awake list`, `--json`, `--no-color` / `NO_COLOR`): plain text and JSON modes for scripts and CI. `awake status` prints a full JSON object with every state field.
- **Status details**: `awake status` shows the active power plan sleep and hibernate timeouts, the screensaver setting and which execution state requests the daemon currently holds (`Requests: system / system + display`).
- **Daemon logging** (`awake log`): rolling log files (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\awake\logs\daemon\daemon-YYYYMMDD.log`, appended across restarts of the same day) with a configurable level and size/file-count limits, hot-applied via RELOAD. `awake log export [path]` packs the log files into a dependency-free .zip for issue attachments. Logging is **enabled by default**.
- **Hardened pipe server**: oversized or malformed requests are dropped safely, remote connections are rejected and the pipe name cannot be hijacked (`FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE`).
- **Elevation guard (option A)**: the daemon refuses to run elevated - a high-integrity pipe cannot be controlled from a normal shell, which left users with an uncontrollable daemon. `daemon on` in an elevated shell fails with a clear error. Automation environments can opt out with `AWAKE_ALLOW_ELEVATED=1`.
- **Watch list and performance**: watched image names are matched case-insensitively, the parsed list is cached by file stat, the process scan stops as soon as every watched name is found, and a vanished `awake.ini` is recreated automatically.
- **Autostart** through the `HKCU` Run key (no administrator rights), with stale-entry detection and repair.

## Full command list

```
awake help               Show the help message.
awake version            Show the version.
awake aliases            Show every command alias.
awake 0                  Disable keep-awake.
awake 1                  Enable keep-awake (blocks idle sleep/hibernation).
awake 1 for <period>     Enable keep-awake for a limited time.
awake 1 until <HH:MM>    Enable keep-awake until that clock time.
awake status             Show daemon, keep-awake, screen, autostart and
                         watch list status.
awake list               List the watched applications (--json for JSON).
awake screen on          Keep the screen on (blocks screen off, screensaver
                         and idle lock).
awake screen on for <period>   Keep the screen on for a limited time.
awake screen off         Stop keeping the screen on.
awake daemon on          Start the background daemon.
awake daemon off         Stop the background daemon.
awake daemon enable      Start the daemon automatically at logon.
awake daemon disable     Do not start the daemon automatically at logon.
awake log                Show or change daemon logging (on / off / level /
                         max-files / max-size / export [path]).
awake reload             Re-read the configuration file immediately.
awake reset              Reset the configuration file (asks for
                         confirmation).
awake add <imagename>    Add an image name to the watch list.
awake del <imagename>    Remove an image name from the watch list.
```

Global options: `--json` makes `list` and `status` machine-readable; `--no-color` (or the `NO_COLOR` environment variable) disables all colors. See `awake aliases` for the shorthand forms.

## Installation

1. Extract `awake.exe` and `awake.daemon.exe` from this package into any folder. Both executables are statically linked and have no runtime dependencies.
2. Run `awake daemon on` (or simply `awake 1`) to start using the tool. The configuration file `awake.ini` is created next to the executables on first use; the first command also asks for the license.
3. Optional: run `awake daemon enable` to start the daemon automatically at every logon.

## Notes

- Keep-awake and screen keep-awake states live in the daemon's memory only; after a daemon restart they are inactive again (a running timed period expires with it).
- Manual sleep - the power button, the Start menu or another program's request - is never blocked. Only idle sleep is.
- The daemon must not run elevated: an elevated shell cannot control a normal daemon afterwards. `AWAKE_ALLOW_ELEVATED=1` overrides this for automation environments.
- Daemon logging is enabled by default; disable it with `awake log off`.
- If you enabled autostart and later move the executables to another folder, `awake status` flags the stale entry and `awake daemon enable` in the new location fixes it.
- Upgrading from a beta: keep the new executables in a new folder rather than overwriting a running installation, then run `awake daemon enable` once so the autostart entry points at the new path.
